public_rationale: On the present-state reading, mid-2025 evaluations back the claim. In Salesforce's CRMArena-Pro, leading LLM agents succeeded about 58% of the time on single-turn tasks and about 35% on multi-turn tasks. In CMU's TheAgentCompany, the best agent completed about 30% of workplace tasks, and long tasks were out of reach. That is not robust, trustworthy agent performance. The first sentence is a definition and is not scored. METR's data shows reliability improving quickly, so the forward-looking reading, that LLMs will never get there, is not settled by this assessment.
limitations: Scored on the present-state reading. The trajectory reading remains open.
Benchmarks may understate or overstate real-world reliability.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Reliable agents require robust, trustworthy AI, and LLMs are not getting us there.

statement.excerpt: Reliable agents may not require “artificial general intelligence”, but they surely require what I called in 2020 “robust”, trustworthy AI. LLMs aren’t getting us there.
statement.document_title: AI Agents have, so far, mostly been a dud

our_interpretation: The first sentence states a requirement. It is a definition, not a fact to test.
The testable part, on my reading: as of the post, LLM-based agents had not achieved robust, trustworthy performance on realistic multi-step tasks.
He named no period, so I use 2025 up to the post date: the latest agent evaluations before the post.
Whether LLMs will ever get there is a separate, forward-looking question that I do not score here.
criteria.support_condition: Evaluations from early-to-mid 2025 showing leading LLM agents failing a large share of realistic tasks, or labs themselves warning that agents are not reliable.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evaluations from the period showing LLM agents completing realistic multi-step tasks reliably, at high success rates.

evidence.excerpt: even leading LLM agents achieve modest overall success rates on CRMArena-Pro, typically around 58% in single-turn scenarios, with performance significantly degrading to approximately 35% in multi-turn settings.
evidence.explanation: In mid-2025 the leading LLM agents failed most multi-turn business tasks. That is not robust, trustworthy performance.

evidence.excerpt: in a setting simulating a real workplace, a good portion of simpler tasks could be solved autonomously, but more difficult long-horizon tasks are still beyond the reach of current systems.
evidence.explanation: In this version the best agent completed only about 30% of workplace tasks. Long-horizon tasks were beyond current systems.

evidence.excerpt: We also measure the 80% time horizon of models (Figure 6) and find a similar trend, though horizons are roughly 5x shorter.
evidence.explanation: Agents were far less capable at high reliability than at 50% reliability. But reliability was improving steadily, which bears on the forward-looking reading Marcus may have intended.
